country.name: Thailand
country.tagline: A 'new latitude' wine country where vines crop twice a year and some are harvested by boat.

stats.note: No OIV wine-production figure; Thailand has perhaps a dozen commercial wineries.

country.overview:
Thailand lies between about 6 and 20 degrees north, far outside the textbook wine belt, yet since the 1990s a handful of wineries have made it the best known of Asia's tropical 'new latitude' wine producers. Grapes first came as a gift: the French embassy of Louis XIV presented King Narai with White Malaga vines in the 1680s. For three centuries they were table fruit.

Two areas lead. Khao Yai, in the hills of Nakhon Ratchasima province about 150 km north-east of Bangkok at 300 to 400 m, is home to GranMonte (founded by Visooth Lohitnavy, whose daughter Nikki trained in Adelaide and became Thailand's first female oenologist) and PB Valley. Hua Hin, on the Gulf coast, is home to Siam Winery's Hua Hin Hills Vineyard, which produces the Monsoon Valley brand and has elephant rides among the vines. Siam Winery, founded in 1986 by Chalerm Yoovidhya of the Red Bull family, also grows grapes in the 'floating vineyards' of the Chao Phraya delta west of Bangkok, raised beds between canals tended and harvested by boat.

Without winter dormancy, vines can be pruned to fruit twice a year. The quality crop ripens in the dry, relatively cool season from December to March; the rainy-season crop is weaker. Chenin Blanc, Shiraz, Colombard and the local Pok Dum grape are the mainstays.

history.title: King Narai's grapes
history.text: The French embassy of Louis XIV presented King Narai of Ayutthaya with White Malaga vines; the grapes were grown as fruit.

history.title: Siam Winery
history.text: Chalerm Yoovidhya founded Siam Winery, later known for the Monsoon Valley brand and its floating vineyards in the Chao Phraya delta.

history.title: Khao Yai estates
history.text: GranMonte and PB Valley built wineries in the hills of Khao Yai, which became Thailand's main fine-wine area and a weekend destination from Bangkok.

country.classification: No appellation system; Thai wines use brand and estate names. Khao Yai producers have promoted a regional identity informally.
country.climate_soils: Tropical monsoon climate with a dry season from about November to April; vines are pruned to ripen in it. Khao Yai's elevation of 300 to 400 m and cooler nights help; soils are mostly sandy loam over clay.

grapes.name: Chenin Blanc
grapes.note: The leading white, fresh and fruity.

grapes.name: Shiraz
grapes.note: The main red at Khao Yai and Hua Hin.

grapes.name: Colombard
grapes.note: A heat-tolerant white used by Siam Winery.

grapes.name: Pok Dum
grapes.note: A local black grape, a table variety also made into wine.

regions.name: Khao Yai
regions.tagline: Thailand's hill-country wine area, a weekend drive from Bangkok.
regions.summary: Vineyards in the foothills of Khao Yai National Park around Pak Chong, at 300 to 400 m, where GranMonte and PB Valley make Chenin Blanc, Viognier, Shiraz and Syrah-based blends.

regions.name: Hua Hin
regions.tagline: Coastal hill vineyards inland from the royal resort town.
regions.summary: Siam Winery's Hua Hin Hills Vineyard, inland from the resort, produces the Monsoon Valley brand from Colombard, Chenin Blanc, Shiraz and Sangiovese.
regions.history: Planted in the early 2000s; the visitor centre opened in 2008.
regions.terroir: Sandy soils, hot and dry for half the year.

sites.name: GranMonte
sites.text: The Lohitnavy family's estate in the Asoke Valley of Khao Yai, planted from 1999. Nikki Lohitnavy, who studied winemaking in Adelaide, became Thailand's first female oenologist; GranMonte's Chenin Blanc and Syrah are among Thailand's most awarded wines.

sites.name: PB Valley Khao Yai Winery
sites.text: A Khao Yai estate founded by Piya Bhirombhakdi of the Singha beer family, one of the first commercial vineyards in the area, known for Shiraz and Chenin Blanc and for its vineyard tours.

sites.name: Hua Hin Hills Vineyard (Monsoon Valley)
sites.text: Siam Winery's vineyard in the hills behind Hua Hin, producing the Monsoon Valley range. Visitors can tour the vines by elephant or bicycle. Grapes are pruned so that the main crop ripens in the dry season.

sites.name: Chao Phraya delta floating vineyards
sites.text: West of Bangkok, Siam Winery grows grapes on raised beds between irrigation canals in the Chao Phraya delta, a traditional system for fruit growing in flood-prone land. The vines are tended and harvested from boats.
